topics.headline: Energy price rebound points to both CPI and HICP rising in July
topics.summary: Germany's flash reading already jumped to 2.8% from 2.3% on an 8.3% energy spike, and renewed Hormuz tensions plus a ~30% oil rally make a similar rebound likely for both US CPI and Eurozone HICP after June's energy-driven dip. Reports land July 31 (Eurozone flash) and August 12 (US CPI).

topics.headline: HY spreads drift wider to 2.77-2.84%, driven by rates not credit stress
topics.summary: High yield OAS has widened modestly (up ~15bps to 278bps) mainly due to a Treasury selloff and rate volatility rather than credit deterioration, with spreads still in the lower third of their five-year range; AI-related hyperscaler debt issuance and elevated capex are a watch item, but no imminent Fed action or credit shock points to a dramatic 30-day break wider.

topics.headline: BTC ETF flows flip positive July 30, but pattern remains fragile
topics.summary: A $233M inflow day led by IBIT snapped a rough four-session, $526M outflow stretch and turned weekly/monthly flows positive, but with July's $205M total the weakest month on record and flows whipsawing between inflows and outflows every few days, sustained net inflows over the next week are far from assured.

topics.headline: VIX plunges 17% off spike high, but Fed uncertainty lingers
topics.summary: VIX dropped to 17.09 (-17.28%) after briefly hitting 20.66 on Fed rate-hold jitters, but new chair Warsh's anti-forward-guidance stance and rising hawkish-hike odds (46.9%) suggest volatility could reassert above its 3-month average within 30 days.

topics.headline: OpenAI, Chevron/Microsoft, NRG deals confirm near-certain YES resolution
topics.summary: Within the past 30 days OpenAI secured 3.2GW from Georgia Power for Project Camellia while Chevron signed a 20-year dedicated power deal with Microsoft and expanded its 4GW behind-the-meter turbine buildout, alongside NRG/LandBridge and Brookfield/Bloom Energy agreements — deal velocity is now essentially weekly, making this question resolve YES with near certainty.
